Class MaskExtractor

java.lang.Object
dev.swordai.core.vision.MaskExtractor
public final class MaskExtractor extends Object
Turns a rendered RGBA frame into the enemy masks. The opponent is drawn with a colour-keyed skin (pure blue head, pure green body); everything else in the frame is discarded.

Only a 16:9 region centred on the crosshair is used and all coordinates are expressed in units of half the frame height, so the result is the same whatever shape the window is. Not thread-safe: use one instance per thread.

    • extract

      public void extract(ByteBuffer rgba, int width, int height, boolean bottomUp, MaskFrame out)
      Parameters:
      rgba - pixels as R,G,B,A bytes, row after row, width * height * 4 bytes from index 0
      bottomUp - true when row 0 is the bottom of the image (OpenGL read-back order)

    • extract

      public void extract(ByteBuffer rgba, int width, int height, boolean bottomUp, float crop, MaskFrame out)
      Parameters:
      crop - the middle part of the frame to use, as a fraction of its height (1 is all of it). The middle of a frame drawn with a wide field of view is exactly the picture of a narrower one, so this lets the screen and the network use different fields of view. Everything reported is relative to the part used, as if it were the whole frame.

    • fill

      private static void fill(int[] count, int[] total, byte[] out)
      Coverage of each cell as 0..255. Cells that fall outside the frame stay empty.
